title: Bus Route & Stops
strapline: Ding the bell, mind the doors — a bus that stops at every child's stop, in the same order every time.
intent: Children learn sequence and routine — the bus visits its stops in a fixed order, every single time.
Children predict what comes next: which stop, who is waiting, how many more until ours.
Children count passengers on and off and keep track of how many are on board.
Children take turns in the roles that make a bus work — driver, conductor, passenger — and cooperate.
Children connect to their own real journeys and the local buses they ride.
implementation: Line up chairs as the bus and set out named bus stops around the room in a route order.
Drive the route and call the stops in the same sequence, asking 'what's the next stop?' before you arrive.
Count passengers on and off at each stop and wonder aloud how many are left on board.
Give the bus a bell to ding, a fare tin, tickets to punch and a destination sign to change.
Rotate the roles openly — everyone gets a turn to drive, conduct and ride.
Add a picture timetable and a map of the route so mark-making and reading have a purpose.
Talk about children's real bus journeys — which number bus, where it goes, who they sit with.
key_questions: What's the next stop on our route — who is waiting there?
How many passengers are on the bus now? How many got off?
How many more stops until we reach the park?
What do you need to do to pay for your ticket?
Which bus do you catch, and where does it take you?

impact.text: Children follow the route in a fixed order and predict which stop comes next.
Children count passengers on and off and track how many are on board.
Children take turns as driver, conductor and passenger and cooperate to run the bus.
Children punch tickets, read the destination sign and mark-make the route with meaning.
Children narrate the journey with journey and position words — next stop, mind the doors, all the way to the end.
Children talk about their own real bus journeys and where the local buses go.

enhancements: Chairs set out as the bus, with a driver's wheel and a bell to ding.
Named bus stops placed around the room in route order.
Tickets, a hole punch, a fare tin and pretend money.
A changeable destination sign and a picture timetable.
A route map to follow, draw and adapt.
Photos of the children's real local buses and stops.
Bags, buggies and shopping so passengers have places to be going.

playing_exploring: Children replay their own bus journeys and invent new destinations.
They explore the roles that keep the bus running.
active_learning: Children keep the route going, stop after stop, to the end of the line.
They concentrate to count the passengers on and off correctly.
creating_thinking: Children predict the next stop and who's waiting there.
They solve the full bus, the missed stop and the lost ticket in role.
